items: Achekaye kilema hata kwao kipo.
One who laughs at a cripple has a family defect too.
A warning to those who laugh at the deformity of another, for they will be punished in the same way.
Afadhali lawama ya wazi.
An open reproach is best.
Afanyae mzaha na watu humlazimu awe na saburi.
People who tease others must have patience for when they'll be teased in turn.
Ajabu ya kondoo kucheka kioo.
How amazing that a sheep mocks its image in a mirror [not knowing that it laughs at its own image].
This is said of someone who is making fun of another, while having the same imperfection or making the same mistake.
Ajabu ya ngamia kuchekanundu ya ng'ombe.
How amazing that a camel derides the cow for its hump.
The camel has a bigger hump.
Akulengaye kisu hashindwi kuchoma.
The one who points a knife at you can stab you.
Akutadiye nawe mtadi.
Do the same to someone who arrogantly insults you.
AkutuKAnaye hakuchagulii tusi.
The one who insults you does not choose insults.
Not mincing words and really trying to hurt you. One who wants to insult you does not lack proclamation.
Akuumizaye ni mtu akujuaye.
The person who hurts you is the person who knows you.
Amefurahi, meno hayaumi mkate.
That one is happy, that person's teeth don't bite the bread.
This is said when somebody in a good mood does not respond to an insult.
Amekuja kwa meno ya juu.
That person came with upper teeth.
With brute force.
Atupaye tope hujichafua naye.
Those who throw mud get soiled as well.
If you throw mud it will jump back to you. That abused person will get back at you.
Baada ya kisa mkasa: baada ya chanzo kitendo.
After a story, a happening: after a beginning, the action. tit for tat - H.
Every happening has a beginning. A counterattack is quick and precise. This proverb is used when people think that something happened without a cause.
Baada ya kovu na jeraha ndani.
Even after it has been covered by scar tissue, the wound still hurts inside.
An insult is not easy to forget.
Biashara haigombi.
Trade does not quarrel.
A businessman is careful in the choice of his words in order not to alienate his customers, and to attract them.
Bila mtu wa pili ugomvi hauanzi.
Without a second person a quarrel cannot start.
Cheka kilema, uzae kilema.
Laugh at a deformed person and you will bear a deformed child.
A warning to stop people from laughing at others, and to show sympathy instead.
Cheka maiti na maiti itakucheka.
Mock a corpse and the corpse [in time] will laugh at you.
Chokoa chokoa yatia meno ubovu.
All that picking makes bad teeth.
A person who annoys you on purpose makes you angry [bad teeth].
Chungu huliita birika "mweusi".
The stone pot calls the aluminum pot black. English proverb: the kettle calls the pot black.
Dhoruba ilipo, shwari ipo.
Where there was a storm, there is calm.
Where there is disturbance, there can be reconciliation followed by calm.
Dhoruba katika kikombe cha chai.
Tempest in a tea cup.
(English import.) To make much of little things. About people who are afraid about little things.
Haifai kumtukana sungura miguu mikubwa na tembo yupo palepale.
Don't laugh at the rabbit's big feet while the elephant is present.
Hekaheka nyuma vita mbele.
After much shouting there will be a fight.
Hujavuka mto, simtukane mamba.
You haven't crossed the river, so don't insult the crocodile.
Iwapo hukutana, ifanye hukusikia.
If people abuse you, pretend you did not hear it.
Jahazi chombo kikuu hakistahimili (or hakihimili) kubisha.
An old sail boat does not tolerate tacking.
An old person does not suffer being moved out or being maneuvered around.
Jani kavu mtini linalilaumu lililo chini kwa kelele.
A dry leaf on the tree blames the leaf on the ground for noise.
It is easy to see other people's faults.
Jirani ndiye ndugu, usimkashifu hata kidogo.
Neighbor is a relative, don't slander him/her even a little.
Jogoo kasema usiku umekucha anikanyagae kakusudia.
The rooster said the day is breaking, so who steps on me does it on purpose.
The fowl staying in the same house might be trod upon by a person going out early. A person doing harm often blames it on the situation.
Jungu humchoma mpishi na mlaji.
Huge pot burns the cook and the eater.
It becomes very hot and difficult to handle. This means that a quarrel often harms the initiator as well as the receiver.
Kaa alimcheka mtoto wake mwendo.
The crab laughs at the way its young one walks.
Kaa hutokotwa na maji yakwe.
Crab is boiled in its own water.
A defenseless person will be cruelly treated.
Kalimba hula samaki wadogo.
The big kalimba fish eats the small ones.
Little people are the victims of big people. Instead of kalimba one could use mbota (Nile perch) or chewa (rock cod) or nguru (king fish).
Kibuzi akafa vigongo.
The kid (young goat) died from blows with a stick.
It became the laughing stock, the scapegoat.
Kidonda kimerudi penye kovu.
The wound returns to the scab.
It remains in the memory. The insult is not forgotten and whatever you do it comes back to you.
Kila dhihaka na mazowea.
Every joke (insult) has its own familiarity.
Kila fitina hakosi kutumika.
Every quarrel is used again.
Kila mcheka kilema naye humsikilia.
Whoever mocks a lame [person], one day it will happen to him.
Kila mwenye choo huenda jaani.
Everyone who has a need goes to the rubbish heap.
All people slander. [The rubbish heap was and is also the latrine, in the middle of a group of houses, to be used collectively].
Kilema hamcheki mwenziwe.
Cripple does not mock a companion.
Kilichoniuma jana nikaona uchunguwe hakinitambai tena.
That which bit me yesterday and hurt me, does not crawl over me a second time.
Kima waliotahiriwa hawatawalani.
Monkeys that have been circumcised [ceremonially cleansed] will not eat you.
Kipofu simcheke, si makosa yake.
Don't laugh at a blind person, it is not that person's fault.
Kisiki unikwaze nipate sababu.
Tree stump, make me stumble, so that I have a motive.
One does not act without reason. If one wants to pick on someone there generally is an aversion or a quarrel. Kakalia kisiki nikwae.
Kitumbua changu sikitie mchanga.
Don't put sand in my cake.
Do not spoil my sport, do not rob my story.
Kobe alikimbia kwa kuchekwa mwendo wake.
The tortoise fled because they laughed at its gait.
A wise person keeps silent when ridiculed.
Kucheka-cheka, kutatoweka.
Laughing, laughing will die away.
People who always laugh at others will get their due.
Kucheka kovu, asiyefikwa na jaraha.
Person who laughs at a scar has not received a wound.
Laughing at peoples' misfortune shows ignorance. Adhihakiye kovu hajaona jaraha.
Kuchuachua, kuchua si kwema: mchomwa mwiba hawi mtembezi.
It is not good to provoke someone all the time.
Kulia kwa samaki, machozi (yake) huenda na maji.
The tears of the fish are carried away by the water.
Suffering of the poor is not considered important.
Kunguni asema chawa anauma zaidi.
The bedbug says the louse's bite is more painful.
The kettle calls the pot burnt black.
Kutoboa-toboa ndiko kujitoboa mwenyewe.
By continual stabbing one stabs oneself.
Always insulting people and mocking them, destroys oneself. Kuchokoachokoa ndiko kujichokoa mwenyewe.
Kuwa mbali kuliana, kuwa karibu magombano.
There is weeping when separated, there is quarreling when together.
Said of friends or relatives who always quarrel when together.
Kwetu dia hailali, si kondo.
In our house revenge sleeps not, no doubt about that.
Laana halifi.
Curse does not die.
Lahaula, yamekufika.
Blasphemy, and it has come to you already.
Kila lahaula hufuatwa na adhabu ya Mungu, every blasphemy is followed by God's punishment.
Élanivuwaza kama shazi jicho la ndugu.
It cuts me like an oyster shell: the [envious] eye of a brother.
The oyster shell cuts the skin [superficially] and hurts: the evil eye of a relative also inflicts pain. This is said about family vendettas.
Lao huwinda pazima ili kupatia pengo. Sacl.
Their [occupation] is to scrutinize a sound place in order to discover a flaw.
This is said of people who pick a petty quarrel with others.
Lekeza kidole, uwashe ugomvi.
Point a finger, start a quarrel.
Lekeza, elekeza: show, point.
Loliondo huvia kimelea kikistawi.
Loliondo tree withers if a parasite thrives on it.
A loliondo tree is very strong, but a parasite sucks the energy of the tree and withers it. Thus a rich person may be destroyed by parasites.
Masengenyo bila msingi huishia hewani.
Slander without foundation ends up in the sky.
Matukano ni pumba za udongo.
Words of abuse are like lumps of clay.
Easy to find and to throw. Words of abuse are [like throwing] a handful of mud. A word of slander does not stay (no more than mud stays on the face).
Mazoea huleta dharau.
Familiarity breeds contempt.
Mbananga chake hana kondo.
If you spoil what is your own you have no quarrel.
Bananga, haribu: to spoil - Sacl.
Mbughudi cha nje hupata cha ndani.
Tale bearer who reports bad things outside, will get it inside.
If you slander people, it will come back to you.
Mchawi huloga kwa nduguye na kwake kuko shwari.
Wizard puts a spell on his brother, but his own place is peaceful.
Mcheka kilema hafi bila kumfika.
Mcheka kilema hafi hakijamfika.
Mchezaji akikosea hulaumu mpiga ngoma.
Bad dancer blames the drummer.
Mchezea zuri, baya humfika.
One who ridicules the good will be overtaken by evil.
A person who laughs at good works, will fall upon bad times.
Mdharau biu hubiuka yeye.
One who ridicules a deformed person becomes deformed.
Biu and biuka from umbua: deform, disfigure.
Mganga wa karibu usimtukane.
Don't insult your neighbor doctor.
You might need a doctor.
Mguu mmoja ukijikwaa, wa pili hucheka.
If one foot stumbles, the other laughs.
Mheshimiwa hakosi.
An honorable person does not err.
If that person errs, the blame is put on someone else, so that person's prestige is not lowered.
Mhini na mhiniwa njia yao moja.
The teaser and the one who is teased are in the same way.
None profits, both are losers.
Miiba njiani wewe mwenye unaikanyaga.
It is you yourself who stepped on the thorns which are on the road.
Don't accuse others of your faults and mistakes. One who commits blunders must blame oneself.
Mkeka ukaliwao na kila mtu.
Mat on which everybody sits.
Insult for a prostitute.
Mkono wenye kilema hauachi matata.
Deformed arm gives constant trouble.
So does a bad person.
Mkwepa ugomvi huota fimbo.
One who avoids a fight will sprout stick marks on the body.
Some quarrels cannot be avoided, stand for your rights.
Mmeza ung'ongo kajiono.
One who swallows a strip of raffia is aware of it.
Even if receiving an affront calmly, that person nevertheless feels it.
Msambe ndisi wajinga, mtutumao kizungu.
Do not say we are stupid, you who employ us in foreign fashion.
Arabs and Europeans have employed Africans and often called them ignorant, but it is the employers who are ignorant of good manners.
Msitukane wakunga na uzazi ungalipo.
Do not abuse midwives while there is a delivery going on.
Do not insult people who might be of use to you one day. Msitukane as well as usitukane (plural and singular are used.) Msitukane wakunga na uzazi haujaisha.
Mtenda husahau, mtendwa hasahau.
The one who inflicts forgets, the one to whom it is done does not forget.
Mti upijwao mawe ni mti wenye matunda.
The tree that people throw stones at is the tree that bears fruit.
Mti usicheke gogo.
Tree shouldn't laugh at the fallen tree trunk.
Mwana-mongwe ali kwao na mchanga hangelile.
If the noble son had stayed home, he would not have eaten sand.
He would not have been abused and humiliated. Let not the cobbler go beyond his last. Hangelile for hangalikula, and ali for yu, attest the antiquity of this proverb.
Mwapiza la nje, hupata la ndani.
One who curses outside gets it inside.
One who curses about something not really his concern, will bring it home to himself - F. Someone who wishes sickness upon another may fall sick himself.
Mwenye kufanya mchuzi, kiungo ni malimau.
In making the gravy, the seasoning is lemons.
Mwenyezi mungu atakushinda kama shinda la ufuta.
Almighty God will reduce you as the leftovers of simsim.
(A curse.) Shinda: the dregs of the sesame seeds after oil has been extracted from them.
Mzaha, mzaha, hutumbuka usaha.
Mizaha mizaha, hutoka usaha.
Mzingire mwana-mbiji.
Turn the sailor to - T.
A double entendre, meaning either Turn the tables upon him, or Bind him with his hands behind his back - T.
Mzizi wa fitina ushakatika.
The root of discord is cut.
Said when a quarrel is over The root comes out of the stem.
Na kutumiana nguvu, lema litakuwa ovu.
By using violence against each other, a good thing [e.g., a marriage] will become evil.
Lema = jema: a good thing.
Na likukerekete! [or] na likuchome!
Let that irritate you! [or] Let that stick in you!
Exclamations after a strong statement: May that stick in your gizzard, you cannot give an answer to that - J. Put that in your pipe and smoke it - T.
Nilimlilia hajaja, akisha kuja humchukiza.
When one is far apart the faults and differences seem small, but when united, disputes reappear at once.
Nungu kipita huacha miiba.
When the porcupine passes, it leaves its prickles behind.
A prickly character causes irritation and quarreling Kipita, akipita: if it passes.
Nyani wanachekana ngoko.
Monkeys make fun of each other's red behind.
Without seeing their own.
Nyigu haumi bure, ila mtu anamchokoza.
Hornet does not sting, except when it is made angry.
Nyoko nyoko kuonana, kuwa mbali kuliana.
When together they insìult each other and when they are apart they cry for each other.
This is said when a partner is sorry for a separation after a dispute.
Nyoko! Nyoko! Ni shiba ya kuonana.
Abuses are the result of seeing one another too often.
Nyumba ya wavuvi.
House of fishermen.
A household with lots of quarrels and fighting - V. A house full of noise.
Osha uso ndipo ua wenje.
Wash your face then come outside.
If you have washed your face, you can laugh at the person who hasn't. Ua wenje = utoke nje: come outside.
Pita na zako.
Go along with your things.
Mind your own business.
Samaha ni rahisi, mwerevu hutafuta sababu.
If forgiveness comes easy, a clever person asks why?
Shuka ya maskini ndiyo itandiwayo dagaa.
The dagaa will be spread out upon the loincloth of the poor.
If anything bad happens, the poor and helpless are blamed.
Si vema, kucheka kilema.
It is not nice to laugh at a cripple.
Tupa tupa tope jingi, baadhi litampata.
If you throw plenty of mud, some of it will stick.
Ubishi mwingi huvuta (or huleta) mateto.
Joking carried too far leads to quarreling.
Ubishi chanzo cha mateto.
Ubishi ulivunja mji wa nyani.
Quarreling broke up the village of the monkeys.
Ukidhihaki shombo humli samaki.
If you joke about fish smell, don't eat fish.
If you laugh at the fishermen smelling badly, you won't get fish.
Ukitaja nyoka, shika fimbo mkononi.
When you mention a snake get hold of a stick.
Ukitaja nyoka, shika kigongo.
Umegeuka kitatange, wachungia wenzio demani?
Have you become a kitatange taking care of your companion in the basket?
Huyo ni kitatange atakutosa demani.
Umwonyeshaye meno, kinywani hukutia kidole.
The one to whom you show your teeth, puts a finger in your mouth.
Unamlaumu mwewe, kipanga yuwesha kuku.
You are blaming the hawk, [while] the falcon is killing the chickens.
Don't blame the one who committed a minor mistake and leave the one who does big harm.
Ushungu mwenenda nao, shingo ujeze matama.
The poison a man bears, has filled [his] cheeks with venom.
T. Treasured malice will out in bitter speeches. T. Not a common proverb.
Usiharibu utu kwa kitu, afadhali haribu kitu kwa utu.
Use things to make you a better human being.
Usilaumu ardhi uliyoangukia, laumu kigingi kilichokukwaza.
Don't blame the ground you fall on, blame the obstacle that causes you to fall.
Don't blame the people where you arrive. If blame is to be given, blame those who sent you there or blame the reason why you are sent there (e.g., prison).
Usilicheke jahazi lililorushwarushwa kwa mawimbi, huenda nduguyo yumo ndani yake.
Don't laugh at the sailboat that is tossed by the waves, perhaps your relative is in it.
Usimcheke kilema ukiwa hai.
Don't laugh at a cripple while you are alive.
Something worse could happen to you.
Usimcheke mkweo, utaota chokea [nene].
Do not laugh at your mother-in-law for you will get a sty in your eye.
Common belief that evil will come to a person who mocks his/her mother-in-law. The remedy consists in rubbing the eye with a garment of the one who has been ridiculed.
Usimcheke mkwezi usikose nazi nyumbani.
Don't laugh at the coconut picker, you might lack coconuts at home.
Usimhamakie mpita njia.
Passerby, don't make him angry.
Even if that person bothers you it is only for a passing moment.
Usimpige mtu akiwa chini.
Don't kick a person who is down.
Low-minded people talk evil of a fallen opponent.
Usimtukane pongo miguu mirefu na kondoo yuko pale.
Don't insult the antelope on account of its long legs, while a sheep is present.
Usipende vita na ukimkuta rafiki kiteta, sichoteÿ amua.
Do not enjoy discord and if you find your friend quarreling do not stir it up, but make peace.
Usishindwe kulala usingizi ukasema kitanda ni kibovu.
Saying that the bed is bad should not stop you from sleeping.
About blaming someone else.
Utamu wa funza kukata kidole.
The delight of the chigger is to cut the toe.
Pleasure to hurt. Creatures follow their nature.
Vinya lakini usifivinye.
Pinch but do not crush.
Vita vya ndugu haviamliki.
Family wars [fights] do not invite.
I.e., do not interfere.
Vitu vya biashara havigombani.
Articles of trade do not quarrel.
There is no harm in selling objects of different kinds. Has probably a deeper meaning as: those who share the same fortune will not fight each other, but join hands.
Wakati wa hari, watu hugombana kisima kimoja.
In the dry season people quarrel over one well.
Wakiwa kuhuji mtu na mkewe, jahazi la saji limevunjiwa pa mawe.
While the man and his wife were arguing, the great ironwood ship was broken on the rock.
While they were bickering over trivialities, their seemingly solid marriage broke up.
Wapenda samaki humbeza mvuvi.
Fish lovers disdain the fisherman.
Watu kuagua ugonjwa, hawaagui [siyo; sio] jeuri.
People cure sickness but do not cure violence.
Waungwana hawagombani.
Gentle folks do not quarrel.
Wema huzaa matusi.
Goodness engenders abuse.
Do good to an evil person and he/she will abuse you.
Wema kumanyoko.
Goodness causes insults.
Yuna uchungu na shingo.
That person has bitter and venomous rejoinders.
Used when someone remembers with malice.
Abiria linda mamba.
Traveller, watch out for crocodiles.
Afadhali kuvunja uchumba kuliko kuvunja ndoa.
It's better to break an engagement than a marriage.
Ajaye kisimani mbele hunywa maji maenge.
The first person coming at the well drinks clean water.
Those coming afterwards will find muddied water. We should not wait for others to start doing things.
Akutanguliaye chanoni hukuzidi tonge.
The one who goes before you to the food platter will get a bigger piece than you.
Use the opportunity.
Alikuwa wapi ni kujitunza.
They who were there are taking care of themselves.
Minding your own business. Being alert.
Aliyejamba, mngoje atakunya.
Beware of those who break wind, they are about to defecate.
This is said if something is going to happen. Someone will fall down or something will give.
Aliyengoja, hawezi kuja.
One who waits cannot come [at all].
One of these days is none of these days.
Aombaye magadi awe na kigae (chake).
One who asks for baking powder [soda] should have a container.
One should cooperate with the help given.
Asazacho mwizi mganga atwae.
What the thief has left for you, take it to the witch doctor [to put a curse on the thief].
When someone has been burgled, the person will call the diviner who will 'find' the thief, for a very big fee. Your friends may cause more damage than your enemies.
Asikuwahi mwomba kibuyo.
Let not the one in need of a gourd precede you.
If you are in need of something you should make your request known early upon arrival, lest somebody coming later gets it. First things first.
Asili ya kuchonga mwiko ni kuchoka kuuungua.
The reason for carving a spoon [to stir the porridge] is being tired of burning [a hand].
Asiye na macho akaazime ya kondoo.
One who has no eyes should borrow the eyes of a sheep.
Don't expect anything from a narrow-minded person.
Asiyejiangalia huishia "ningalijua.".
Person who does not look out [is careless] will end up [saying] If I had known.
Asiyekuwapo na lake halipo.
One who is not there, nothing of that person is there.
If you are absent you lose your share. You have to be present at the division of an inheritance. Leave no business to others.
Asiyepo haangukiwi.
Those who are not there will not have anything falling on them.
Atahiriwapo mtoto (or mwana)wa mtemi, na wa maskini.
Atahiriwe papo hapo.
Baada ya kifo ni tabibu.
After death, the doctor.
When it is too late one looks for the remedy. In the same vein: baada ya nyama haradali.
Badiliko kwa mjukuu uanze na babu.
Change needed in a grandchild has to begin with the grandfather.
Start early.
Bahati ikibisha (or ikipiga) hodi ni sharti ufungue mlango mwenyewe.
When fortune knocks at the door, you have to open the door yourself.
For example: If there is a vacancy for employment, don't wait until you are called, but go after it.
Bila [kumshinda] nyuki hupati asali.
Without [overcoming] bees you cannot get honey.
Bila silaha usiingie vitani.
Don't join in a fight if you have no weapons.
Don't start anything without making adequate preparations.
Bilauri si kopo.
[drinking] glass is not worth a [tin] cup.
It's nicer but is easily broken. Beauty versus performance.
Boriti ikianguka, boriti mpya ikaze.
When a roof beam falls, fix a new one.
This may refer to a widow or widower.
Bunde haviziwi kwa nyuma.
An owl is not caught from behind.
An owl is always looking. It is not easy to challenge a brave person.
Chachu kidogo huumua mkate.
Little yeast raises the loaf.
A small fire destroys a big forest.
Chelewa-chelewa utamkuta mwana si wako.
For always postponing you discover that the child is not yours.
Chura akitupwa majini hafi.
If a frog is thrown into water it doesn't die.
This means that a person may believe to have punished somebody while in fact one has done a favor to that person.
Chura aliapo maji yangali machache, yakijaa halii.
Frog in shallow water does not cry when the water is high.
The frog cries because there is something important going on, e.g., fighting in parliament about something valuable. The frog does not cry when all is well.
Dalili ya mvua [ni] mawingu.
The sign of rain is clouds.
Watch out for early warning signs.
Dama ni ilo mkononi.
The sailing rope is in [your] hand.
E, kengewa lolo, kipata nyakua.
You swift kite, if you find [a chicken] grab it.
Make use of the opportunity when it comes.
Enenda kwa tasihili wala usitaghafali.
Go quickly [when you are sent on an errand] and never be negligent.
Enga kabla ya kujenga.
Take care before building.
Think carefully about the results and possibilities of your actions. Enga= angalia: consider.
Fanya fundo kwa siku ya mashaka.
Make a knot for the day of distress.
Swahili people used to keep their money in a knot in a corner of their garment. Provide against a rainy day.
Fedha haiwezi kununua "kama ningejua".
Money cannot buy if only I had known. Missed opportunity.
Fimbo iliyo mkononi, ndiyo iuayo nyoka.
The stick in the hand is the one that kills the snake.
Often there is no time to look for a weapon, when confronted with a snake.
Fimbo ya mbali haiui nyoka.
The stick which is far [not at hand] does not kill the snake.
Fua chuma wakati kingali na moto.
Strike the iron while it is still hot.
Haidhuru hudhuru.
Never mind brings harm.
Carelessness is dangerous. If something shows signs of going wrong, it should be rectified immediately so that it can bring no harm.
Hajikwai mtu kwenye mlima, hujikwaa kwenye kilima cha fuko.
People do not stumble over a mountain, they stumble over a molehill.
It's easier for a person to stumble over an insignificant matter than over a significant one.
Hala hala - mti na macho.
Watch out - a tree and eyes.
A warning: Timber! Alaala or halahala: expression of annoyance, impatience.
Hamadi [ni iliyo] kibindoni, silaha [ni] iliyo mkononi.
Translates freely: By the Prophet!
I have some cash on me, is as good as having a weapon ready in one's hand in time of need. Only what you have in hand can be relied on.
Hapa si pale.
Here is not there.
Hauchi, hauchi, unakucha.
It does not dawn!
It does not dawn! . It dawns! Certain things will happen, even if you believe they will not happen - L. Time and tide wait for nobody.
Hayawi, hayawi, huwa.
They are not happening, they are not happening ... they happen.
Hiari na kitari ni yako.
The choice and preference is yours [your final decision].
In the last resort you have to decide for yourself.
Hofia kijacho.
Fear for what is coming.
Prepare for the future.
Huisha vizuri kianzwacho vizuri.
What is begun well, ends well.
Huyaondosha mavi yangali fukuto; yakiisha oza ni magumu.

Ideas are picked up in a meeting [of brains].

Bamba na waume.

From contradictory advice a peaceful solution is born.

To put a person on his/her seat.
To stop someone's evil doing.
Kuambiana kupo, kusikilizana hapana.

Especially when there are warnings involved.

Mkutano wa vyura.

Don't give advice to a crowd.
It's useless.
Waonywapo ndipo waonapo.
Where people are warned there also is understanding.

Take the second best.

Better half an egg than an empty shell.

Hata simba hula majani.

Huishi kama ameingia peponi.

Said of a lazy, careless person.

Kila mtu na roho yake.
Every person with his/her own soul (or character).

Fistful of water is sufficient for a child to drink.

Whether you have little or much, be content.
Kwenu ni kwenu japokuwa porini.
Your home is your home, even in the wilds.
Kwetu kwanifaa zaidi.

There is no place like home.
Maji meupe baharini, lakini pwani hayanishi nyota.

Mbaazi ukikosa maua husingizia jua.

It's hard to accept one's own shortcomings.
Mbwa apendelee mifupa.
Dog ought to prefer bones.

It's the nature of mankind never to be satisfied.

Nyosha miguu kadiri ya kitando chako.
Stretch your legs according to your bed.
Be content with what you have.
Nyumba ya nyuni, haioni nduni.
The bird does not think that its own nest is shabby.
Padogo pako si pakubwa pa mwenzako.

Si, is not. In proverbs the si means that the first part of the sentence is more important than the second part.
Penda chako.
Love what is yours.
Penye mvua, dungu hutuficha.

Be content with this which you have, this which ties your house together [i.e., the family].

Imekuwa vuta nikuvute.

Kinga na kinga, ndipo moto uwakapo.
Firebrand on firebrand, then the fire burns.

Kiraka cha jamvi ni kanda.

Kukataa kwa chungu ni kuvuja.

Agreeing with the neck sideways.

Kwenye makaa bila moto hakukauki nyama.
Dead coals don't cure meat.

Neighbors help one another.
Mambo kikowa.

Mfanya na mfanyiwa.

Mkono mmoja haubebi mtoto.

Mmoja hashui chombo.

Msaidie anayekusaidia.
Help the person who helps you.

Mti hauendi ila kwa nyenzo.

About common effort. Could also be applied to bribery: One who greases thewheels helps his oxen. Mti hauendi ila kwa mwao.

Kushulika from shua, to launch a boat.
Mti pekee haujengi.
One builds nothing with one tree only.
Mti ukigwa huegemea mti wenziwe.
When a tree falls it leans on its neighbor.
One looks to one's friend in adversity.
Mwenye kubebwa hujikaza.
One who is carried [on the back] must cling on.

Mwenye lake usimngoje na lako.
Don't expect that someone with trouble will cater for yours.
Mwewe hana mihadi na kuku.

Paka wengi wangewako, wamewazidisha panya.

Penye uzia penyeza rupia.
Inject money where there is a problem.

Penye wanaume wengi hapaugui mwana.

The trouble of a relative is solved by a relative.

Tendegu moja halisimamishi kitanda.

So, don't get in that situation.
Ukuni mmoja hauwaki mekoni.

[good] farmer does not forget the old worn out hoe.

Better one in the hand than ten in the bush.

Health is priceless.

Mganga wa miti shamba. A native doctor with local medicine.
Mgonjwa akiugua sana, si lazima afe.
Even a very sick person does not necessarily die.
Mgonjwa haulizwi dawa.
Sick person is not asked if he wants a remedy.
Just give what is needed.
Mgonjwa mwenziwe ni kitanda.
Bed is the companion of a sick person.
Mtambua ndwele ndiye mganga.
The person who recognizes the illness is the physician.
Only when a person recognizes the cause of trouble can it be cured.
Mtoto akitotukuta si mzima.
If a child does not jump about, it is not healthy.
Mtu ni afya.
Person is health.
Mwenye tende hana paja.
A person suffering from elephantiasis has no lap [for a child to sit on].
Tende, teende: A thick or swollen leg. The person does not feel pain. This sickness is common in cold and damp places e.g. on Pemba island - Krapf.
Nduli na mchimba dawa shauri lao ni moja.
The angel of death and the pharmacist [the root-digger] are in accord.
The object of both the digger of medicines and the angel is one, viz., to relieve the afflicted one - T. Death and the doctor, their counsel is the same - T.
Ng'ombe mteua jani ni mgonjwa.
Cow that chooses grass is sick.
Pumu zimepata mkohozi (or kikohozi).
The one who has a cold gets emphysema.
A person who is weak will get a greater sickness.
Shibe ya waganga hutoka kwa wagonjwa.
The bounty of the physician comes from the sick.
Sitafuga ndwele na waganga tele.
I shall not suffer illness while doctors abound - F.
Tunza maji ya kisima, jamaa wawe wazima.
Take good care of the well so that the family may be well.
Ugonjwa hufichwa lakini kifo hakifichiki.
Sickness can be hidden, but death cannot be hidden.
Ugonjwa ni mmoja, matabibu wana tofauti ya elimu.
Sickness is one [is the same], but the doctors differ in their science.
Ugonjwa wa moyo aujua mgonjwa.
The sickness of the heart is known by the patient.
Ukiona ndwee ikishindana na dawa, mganga sijisumbue, pana jambo litakuwa.
When you see a disease struggling with medical treatment, doctor, don't be upset, something will happen.
Ukiwaa (or ukiugua) uwe na subira.
If you fall ill, have patience.
Recovery will take longer than you think. Waa (Lamu dialect),ugua: to be ill.
Umeingiwa mti.
The tree has been overtaken.
A powerful person is sick.
Usipouguza mwele una koo la ujuko.
If you do not look after a patient you will have a family of the shroud (i.e., all your relatives will die).
Uzee hauna dawa.
There is no cure for old age.
Uzima haubadilishwi mali.
Life [health] and wealth are not bartered.
Uzima wa akili ni mwili.
The health of the brain is related to the body.
Achari yalisha.
Pickles cause [the guests] to eat.
A request must be couched in pleasant terms. Achari, appetizer.
Akomelepo mwenyeji na mgeni koma papo.
Where the host has stopped, there the guest stops also.
When the host is convinced about something, the guest stops arguing.
Akufukuzaye hakwambii toka.
One who chases you away does not tell you leave. Do not wait until you are told.
If you are not welcome, stay away. The visitor must be careful not to overstay his welcome. If one wants to be without you, that person will not tell you: get out!
Akuwingaye kwake hakwambii ndokea, hukutendea vitendo ambavyo vya kukuchukia.
One who expels you does not tell you go away, but he'll treat you unkindly.
Heri yako heri yangu.
Your happiness is my happiness.
Said to a guest.
Karibu mgeni, lakini humwekei macho.
Invite the stranger but do not scrutinize him.
Kumwekea macho, put the eyes on somebody.
Kazi haina ugeni.
Work knows no guest.
When a guest arrives at the host's, the guest gets time to be entertained and to rest.
Kuku mweupe ni hatari kwa usalama.
White chicken is a danger for security and peace.
A white chicken stands out in the village, and so does a stranger. That easily upsets the tranquility of the village. A white fly. A red herring.
Kula ni faradhi ya kila mtu.
Eating is the right of everybody.
Nobody must ever be refused food.
Kusimama ingali kwenda.
Standing and still going.
Said if somebody is invited to come in and to sit down, but keeps on standing and talking.
Kutu kuu ni la mgeni.
Old rust is for the visitor - F.
The host brings out his best things, not normally used. The expression Kupokewa kwa mikono miwili, to be received with open arms.
Maji! Ni kumbwe na kinyweo! Matupu yasonga moyo.
You offer me water to drink.
That is all right, but you know water on an empty stomach is hard on the heart.
Mgeni hachomi chaza mtaani akanuka.
Stranger does not roast an oyster in a village and then get accused of smelling of it - F.
A visitor, even when roasting an oyster in a village, will not be told that it smells. A stranger should be excused for strange ways - F.
Mgeni hachukui nyumba.
Guest does not take over the house.
Mgeni na mwenyeji.
The visitor and the owner.
Omitted is husaidiana, help each other.
Mgeni naje mwenyeji apone.
May the guest come and bring some relief to the host.
The arrival of a guest is a blessing. It is usual for a guest to bring his host some present - F. The host will often invite friends and neighbors.
Mgeni ni kuku mweupe.
Stranger is like a white chicken.
And is very noticeable - F. The new wife is the center of attraction. Don't become a white chicken. Becoming different from the others. Showing off.
Mgeni ni maji ya mvua.
Visitor is like rain [does not stay].
But also a visitor is welcome like rain in a scorched land.
Mgeni ni mtumwa wa mwenye nyumba.
Visitor is the slave of the owner of the house.
In a strange environment one acts subdued.
Mgeni pofu ingawa ana macho yake.
Stranger is blind even if the visitor has eyes.
If the visitor sees bad or unpleasant things nothing must be said.
Mgeni siku mbili, ya tatu mpe jembe.
Guest two days, the third give him a hoe.
Do not exceed your hospitality.
Mgeni wa mvua hafukuzwi, mwache aweke mzigo wake.
Visitor arriving in the rain is not refused entry, let him put down his load.
Mkarimu humchinja mkirimiwa.
Host kills the guest.
Mwenda kwao hafungwi mlala.
Somebody going home is not fastened to a palm-strip.
A parting guest must not be loaded with commissions. It was customary for a person going home to tie a palm-strip on the arm in reminder of an errand given by the host.
Mwenye kuwa na mgeni haoni mwezi mwandamo.
One who lodges a visitor does not see the appearance of the new moon.
The host must not alert the visitor to the passing days.
Njoo mgeni uponye mwenye nyumba.
Welcome guest and save the host.
All will enjoy delicious food and quarrels will be put to rest.
Nyumba yangu ni joya, atakaye huingia.
My house is like a spongy coconut, anyone who likes goes into it.
Everyone is welcome. My house attracts profiteers.
Pema usijapo pema, ukipema si pema tena.
Familiarity breeds contempt.
Ukipema probably uki-pa-ima, if you stay there.
Shereheka na mgeni wako kama vile ambavyo ungependa ushereheshwa ugenini.
Celebrate with your visitor as much as you would like to be celebrated as a visitor.
Siku njema ni zawadi ya msafiri.
Good day is the gift of a traveler.
A polite phrase of welcome.
Simlishe paka wa jirani, atavunja kombe na sahani.
Do not feed the neighbor's cat, it will break cups and saucers.
Be careful whom you invite. One who interferes in other people's business is in danger of being accused of causing harm or damage.
Tabasamu hushibisha.
Smile satisfies hunger.
Even if there is little food, if the host gives it with an open and happy heart, the guest will be satisfied.
Uchwewapo [na jua], lala.
When you are overtaken by the sunset, sleep.
This saying is often said in combination with: Ushikwapo shikamana.
Ugeni mbaya kukosa jirani.
Being a stranger is bad, you have no neighbor to turn to for help.
Unapopokea mgeni, usifunge uso.
When you receive a visitor, don't frown.
Usipangue fanicha ukingali mgeni.
Don't rearrange the furniture while you are a visitor or a newcomer.
When new to a place, don't start changing things before you have studied the situation. Fanicha, furniture.
Usivunje [hata] mguu wa kuku.
Do not break [even] a chicken's leg.
Nobody is allowed to take liberties with the wife of the host.
Ajizi nyumba ya njaa.
Indecision is the house of hunger.
Uvivu [ni] nyumba ya njaa.
Akilaye ndiye aandikiwaye.
The one who eats it (i.e., the food) is the one for whom it was destined.
Akosaye la mama, atalamwa la mbwaye.
One that is not suckled by his/her mother, will have recourse to a bitch.
A man without a good wife will seek the company of bad women.
Ashibaye hamjui mwenye njaa.
One who has had a full meal does not know the hungry person.
One judges others according to oneself, or one does not know how the other feels. One cannot know the hardship of others until one has experienced them.
Binadamu huongozwa na tumbo.
Human being is lead by his stomach.
Chafi rasilimali yake utumbo.
The belonging of the chafi- is its stomach.
Said of somebody who eats ferociously. Chafi or tafi, a kind of broad black fish. Rasilimali, treasure, capital, fortune, property.
Chakula ni uhai.
Food is life.
Deni la tumbo halilipiki.
The debt to the stomach can never be paid.
Every day the stomach demands more. Said of paupers.
Hana njaa fisi, kwani hula najisi.
The hyena is not hungry, because it eats unclean food.
Do not be fastidious.
Hutushiba na harufu wala mnukio.
Yo íu will not be satisfied with the fragrance of the food.
Jamaa kubwa haina chakula kibaya.
In a large family no food is bad.
They value any food they can get and don't waste it.
Kikuponzacho ni tumbo.
That which exposes you [to danger] is your stomach.
The stomach commands the Swahili merchants, fishermen, sailors, and drivers to go out on dangerous journeys to earn their living.
Kila kifaacho huliwa, lakini si kila kiliwacho kinafaa.
Every useful thing is eaten, but not everything that is eaten is useful (good).
Kula (or kila) apataye hajui mwenziwe.
One who obtains food [wealth] does not know his/her companions.
Sucessful people forget their poor old friends.
Kula bakisha njaa, kesho ule tena.
Eating keep a little hungry, tomorrow eat again.
Eat with moderation.
Kula hakuishi.
Eating never ends.
Kula kitu ni riziki.
Eating is a God-given necessity of life.
Kula kupindukia ni kudhoofisha tumbo.
Eating meals in turn in each other's places weakens the stomach.
One does not get his usual food and sometimes the others forget their promise of serving food.
Kula mnapenda mkiambiwa kulima ng'ang'a !
You like to eat, but when you are told to hoe you dry up.
Kula nala kushiba sishibi.
I ate but did get no satisfaction.
Kula na wenzio.
Eating is with friends.
Kula ni faradhi, kufa ni wajibu.
Eating is a duty, dying is a necessity.
Kula sana siyo kushiba.
To eat a lot is not the same as being satified.
Kula siyo kujaza tumbo.
Eating is not the same as filling the belly.
One who eats least eats most, will live longer.
Kula uishi, usiishi kula.
Eat to live, do not live to eat.
Kula ulishe milio, roho nayo ipe mlo.
Eating you feed your body, but give also some food to your soul.
Kula upesi upesi, heshima huinukusi.
Eating in a hurry will diminish your reputation.
Nukusu, nakusi, diminish.
Makao ya njaa ni tumbo.
The dwelling place of hunger is the stomach.
Matikiti na machango ndiyo maponyea njaa.
Melons and gourds, these are the ones which help people through famine.
Honor the people you lived with, and who helped you when you were poor and in need of help. Melons and gourds are blessings of the house. This refers to children.
Mchuzi sio chakula.
Sauce is not food.
Mla chake hana aibu.
If you eat your own [food], you do not have to be ashamed.
Mla na kijiko hajui mla na mikono huchomeka.
One who eats with a spoon does not know that the one who eats with his/her fingers has been hurt.
Mtu mbuge hawezi nyumba.
Compulsive eater cannot manage a home.
About spending all on food. Mbuge, someone who is constantly nibbling on food.
Mwenye njaa hana miiko.
A hungry person observes no taboos.
A starving person is excused to eat any kind of food.
Mwenye njaa hakandiki nyumba.
Hungry person does not plaster the house.
That person is not interested in improving the house. First things first.
Ndege asiyeruka hufa njaa.
A bird that does not fly dies of hunger.
If its food supply is exhausted in its immediate dwelling place, it dies. A person must move to where he can survive.
Njaa haimjui mlimaji.
Hunger does not know the farmer.
Hunger is unknown to the farmer. The farmer does not suffer hunger. Result of his labor.
Njaa haina ndugu.
Hunger has no relative.
Nobody comes to the hungry person.
Njaa iumapo mbwa, mkonowa utarambwa.
When hunger hurts the dog[s], [then] will my hand be licked.
Low-class people will only be polite when forced by need.
Njaa ya leo ni shibe ya kesho.
Hunger today, abundance tomorrow.
Hope is the poor person's bread - V. Hope keeps the heart from breaking - V.
Njaa si bora kuliko shiba.
Hunger is not better than satiety.
Nyama ya koroma sio ya kulika, kabula ya nazi halijakatika.
The flesh of the koroma (an unripe coconut) is not edible before the ripe coconut has been cut.
The elder daughter has to be married off first.
Nyenje inajaa bonde na sikio, nyenje haijai tumbo na vilio.
The cicada fills the valley and the ear with its noise, but it does not fill the stomach.
Pangu pakavu, tia mchuzi.
Put some gravy on my dry portion.
Someone who has a good reputation must expect some evil criticism and maligned curiosity. About enjoying life without caring about the neighbor.
Papigwapo domo kuna njaa.
Babbling is the source of hunger.
Penye njaa hapana haki.
Where there is famine, there is no justice.
It is difficult for hungry people to remain calm. Mwenye uwezi hupata. Those who are able win the day. Those in power will obtain.
Penye njaa, shibe ndiyo kweli.
Where there is famine, food is the truth.
Anything a hungry person is told does not satisfy. Food for that person is truth or real.
Samli ya pemba haimpati mtu macho.
Butter from Pemba does not get a person's eyes.
If somebody is well fed, that does not still another person's hunger - T. Something imported from afar cannot be afforded by many people, so it cannot harm them.
Shiba ya mtu hainilazi na njaa.
Mnene (well fed or fat) instead of njaa.
The repletion of another does not help me to sleep when hungry.
Shiba (or shibe) ya uji yajua mpozi.
The satiety of porridge knows the blower [lit., the cooler] - T.
The person who has had plenty of gruel does not blow at the spoon or cup like the person does who is still hungry - T.
Siku ya kushiba, kumbuka siku ya njaa.
The day you are wll fed, remember the day you went hungry.
Simba akizidiwa nyama hula majani.
If a lion can not eat meat, it will eat grass [weeds].
Tumbo haina inga.
The stomach knows no day of rest.
Inga (Maniema dialect), rest.
Tumbo haiwezekani.
The stomach is invincible.
Hunger must be satisfied.
Tumbo lenye njaa halisikii kengele.
Hungry stomach does not hear the bell.
It neglects duties and timetables. An empty stomach can't fight with other things.
Tumboni hamna mfupa.
There is no bone in the stomach.
A hungry person is weak.
Ukishiba kwa chakula himidi mwenye jalali.
When you are satisfied with your food, praise God's majesty.
Ukishiba usimwonyeshe mung¸u tumbo.
When you are satiated, don't show God your belly.
Don't boast about your possessions and accomplishments.
Ukisikia mtu, ni kula.
If you hear somebody, it's eating.
Eating is necessary for men's survival and is on the foreground of men's conversation.
Ulacho ndicho unukiacho.
You smell according to what you ate.
People know you by the friends you stay with.
Ulapo ndipo penye fadhili yako.
Where you eat there is your commitment.
You are bound/obligated to those who feed you.
Usidharau ukilacho.
Don't despise what you eat.
Uvivu na njaa ni ndugu pacha.
Laziness and hunger are twins.
Vya wahindi haviliwi, vinaliwa kwa harufu.
Indian foods are not eaten, they are enjoyed for their flavor.
Nobody expects to be invited by people of an upper class.
Aendaye polepole hana budi afikile.
The person who walks with calm and care will arrive without fail.
This proverb is illustrated by the story of the tortoise and the hare.
Aliye mbele huja nyuma.
The one who is in front usually comes behind.
Ametia mbugi miguuni.
Some people put bells on their legs.
Are in a hurry. Mbugi, a collar with bells.
Apendaye kula wali husubiri mpunga kuiva.
One who likes to eat rice will wait patiently for the rice to be ripe.
Wali, cooked rice. Mpunga, rice in the paddy. Michele, uncooked rice.
Asubiriye hajuti.
Patient person will not regret.
Bi.kidumu, usikukurike, mwenye safari ni ndoo.
Ee, earthen pot don't take it too seriously, it's the bucket that goes on the journey [to the well].
It is possible that this proverb is intended for the wives of polygamists, whose expectations are not fulfilled. Kidumu kukulika msafari mbeketi.
Chungu kiinjike moto ukiishawaka.
Place the pot on the stones after you've lit the fire.
Set not your loaf in till the oven is hot.
Dafu mtu wa halafu.
Young coconut, a person afterwards.
Everything has its time.
Daraja livuke ulifikiapo.
Cross the bridge when you come to it.
Endambio hashikiki.
[Mr/Mrs.] Run-fast cannot be caught.
Endambio, a composite of enda (go) and mbio (fast).
Hakuna subira mbaya.
There's no bad patience.
Subira, or saburi, patience, resignation.
Haraka, haraka, haina baraka.
Haste, haste has no blessing.
Haste makes waste. Ka ka ka ka haina mbaraka.
Haraka haraka ilimfanya chura akose mkia.
The great haste caused the frog to lose its tail.
Refers to a story.
Haraka kupanda, haraka kushuka.
Climbing in haste, coming down in haste.
A person who suddenly becomes successful may fall suddenly. Maybe the time of that person's rise was too short to learn the skills needed. Hasty climbers have sudden fall.
Harara bila daraka ni barabara bila daraja.
Zeal without responsibility is like a road without a bridge.
Zeal without knowledge is like a runaway horse. Enthusiasm in doing something without caring about the consequences is as dangerous as driving on a road without a bridge.
Heri kawa ufike kama karibu harabu.
Better arrive late than early and so meet, or cause, ruin.
Hulimbikwa nazi juu ya minazi.
The coconuts are left on the trees.
Until they are ripe. Be patient. Do not try to do something too early. Limbika, put aside to grow in ripeness.
Hungojei faranga mbili na nusu.
Don't expect that they will give you back two and a half francs.
Kawia ufike.
Better delay and get there.
The important thing is to reach your goal.
Kilicho baharini kalingoje ufuoni.
What has fallen into the sea, go and wait for it on the beach.
What is lost at sea, go and wait for it on the beach.
Kobe hatavunjika mguu akitembea.
A tortoise will not break a leg in walking.
It walks so slowly.
Kobe yufikile, akenda kwa pole.
The tortoise has arrived, going carefully.
Kukimbia si kufika.
Running is not the same as reaching your destination.
The race is not [always] to the swift.
Kulimatia si kazi, kifungo ni salamini.
Delaying is easy, and the end is in peace.
Never hurry. Limatia, be delayed, be late.
Kusimamia haki ni subiri.
To stand up for justice needs patience.
Kutinda kanzu mwana hajazawa.
To cut out the tunic before the child is born.
Hutafutaje jambia na mtoto hajazawa?
Kutojali saburi, ni kujichimbia kaburi.
Not caring to wait is like digging your grave.
Kuvumilia kugumu matunda yake matamu.
Enduring hardship produces sweet fruit.
Kuvumilia ni kukomaa.
Forbearance is maturity.
It is not easy for a person to have forbearance, but a mature person practices forbearance in all circumstances.
Kumngojesha mtu kwataka sababu.
To keep a person waiting a reason is needed.
Kuzaa kwa haraka mbwa alizaa kipofu.
In being in too great a hurry the bitch gave birth to a blind puppy.
Kwa kukimbia mno mvua, mtwa akajichoma mti.
Running away too hastily before the rain, the Pygmy hurt his foot at a tree.
Mtwa, kibete, mbilikimo, mumbote, a Pygmy.
Kwanza kwa saburi, kwisha kwa sururi.
Begin with patience, end with pleasure.
Kwenda mbio si kufika.
Running in not [necessarily] arriving.
Kwenda pole, huenda kule.
Going slowly [is] going far.
Caution travels a long way. This proverb is illustrated by the story of the tortoise.
Linaloinuka haraka ndilo linalokimbia.
What jumps up in a hurry is what escapes.
Be prepared.
Lumbi haendi dhalali.
The chameleon does not go astray, does not walk in error.
A chameleon can be seen to tread very carefully wherever it goes. Dhalala, being lost, wandering.
Mambo yamwistawia mwenye saburi.
Matters work out better for a person who has patience.
Mawindo ya kwanza hayaui na ya pili hayajarudi.
The first hunt caught nothing and the second party has not yet returned.
So, do not count them yet as successful.
Mbegu za leo si miti ya kesho.
Seeds planted today are not trees tomorrow.
One must have patience.
Mbio za kobe (or kasa) si mbio lakini zakufikisha uendapo.
Tortoise's running is not running, but it helps you reach where you are going.
Mbio za sakafuni huishia ukingoni.
Running on a smooth floor finishes at the edge - F.
Running upon a flat roof will end at the brink.
Mchakacho ujao, haulengwi na jiwe.
One does not throw a stone at an approaching crunching sound.
Wait and see what it is.
Mia - chanzo chake ni moja.
One hundred - it begins with one.
Mimba ya pili haizaliwi kabla ya kwanza.
The second pregnancy does not mature before the first.
One cannot advance or skip certain events.
Mkamate mamba kabla ya kuuza ngozi yake.
Catch the crocodile before selling its skin.
Mso utahamilivu, hali matunda mabivu.
Person that has no patience eats no ripe fruit.
Mstahamilivu hula mbivu.
A patient person eats ripe [fruit].
A patient person eats well cooked [food]. It takes a long time for a seed to bear fruit and waiting is not enough, the tree has to be protected.
Mtafitafi hula swi, mtulivu hula nyama.
Restless person eats fish, but a reliable person eats meat.
A person too much in a hurry. Swi or samaki, fish. Mtafitafii, a blabber, go-between, tale-bearer.
Mvumbika changa hula mbovu.
One who stores half-grown fruit eats the rotten.
Do not pick unripe fruit because it will rot. But also: mvumbika mbichi hula mbivu.
Mwacha kiwi hanacho na chema kimpotele.
If one throws away a bad thing a good thing will also be missed.
If you threw it away before you had the good thing. Kiwi or kibaya, something bad. Kimpotele, kimempotea, escaped somebody.
Mwana hazaliwi mpaka kwa siku zake.
Child is not born before its days.
Mwenda kasi mngojee achoke.
Wait for the fast walker to tire [and then pass him by].
Don't lose your time competing with those who are in a hurry. Used to show that an overactive person does not achieve much and is often a loser.
Mwenda mbio huagana na nyonga.
RunnerS must be in good relation with their hips.
If we want to undertake something, we must make sure that we can realize it. Don't do things beyond your power. Agana or patana, sikilizana, be in agreement.
Mwenda mbio (or haraka) hujikwaa dole.
Person in a hurry stubs a toe.
A careful traveler goes far.
Mwenda-mbizi nchi kavu huuchunua usowe.
Those who dive on dry land graze their face.
Mwenda polepole, hakwai kidole.
Going slowly does not [even] hurt a toe.
And if he/she stumbles it does not hurt. The prudent walker needs no doctor.
Mwenye pupa hadiriki kula tamu.
Hasty person misses the sweet things.
One who eats in a hurry, does not enjoy the taste of food. Work in a hurry does not satisfy anybody.
Ndege mpole akijikwaa havunji mguu.
If a careful bird stumbles, it does not break a leg.
Ngoja kuche si mbali.
Wait dawn is not far.
Said to someone in trouble.
Ngoja, ngoja, ikamkosesha sokwe mkia.
By waiting too long, the chimpanzee missed its tail.
Based on the story that when God was giving tails to all animals, the monkey waited too long to appear. This is said when somebody postpones the fulfillment of a promise.
Ngoja! Ngoja! Haijazi tumbo moja.
Wait, wait! does not fill even one stomach.
Ngoja! Ngoja! Huumiza matumbo.
Wait! hurts the stomach.
Ngoja, ngoja, mtoto si wako.
If you wait too long your girl will sleep with another man.
Ni heri kujizuia, kusubiri ndio njia.
It is good to control oneself, patience is the best way.
Nyikani ukikimbia, nyoka atakuuma.
If you run through the high grass, a snake will bite you.
Pole pole ni [ndio] mwendo.
Being careful is moving ahead.
Also a political slogan: Pole pole ndio mwendo, siasa ya wazalendo. Careful is the political move of the inhabitants.
Pole pole ugali hupikwa.
Slowly, slowly, the porridge is cooked.
Polepole ya kobe humfikisha mbali.
The slow gait of the tortoise takes it far.
Saburi, heshima nusu ya hekima.
